title: Developer Experience Documentation Playbook: SDK Guides, Quickstarts, API Examples, and Support Fixes
author: Ava Thompson
body:
Overview

This playbook defines the standard structure, templates, and operating procedures for Developer Experience (DevEx) documentation at Redwood Inference. It covers SDK guides, quickstarts and templates, canonical API examples, docs-site operating procedures, and the canonical top-support-issue fixes that should be used by support and engineering when troubleshooting customer problems. The goal is to provide consistent, high-quality, on-ramp docs that reduce time-to-first-success for users and lower support load.

Scope

- Audience: external developers, internal solutions engineers, and support engineers.
- Content types: SDK reference guides, step-by-step quickstarts, language-specific examples (Python/Node/Go/cURL), reusable templates, and canonical fixes for the most common support issues.
- Not in scope: internal team meeting notes, experimental drafts (use Google Drive for work-in-progress).

Owner and Review Process

- Doc owner: Developer Experience (DevEx) team in Engineering.
- Primary owner (contact): Ava Thompson (author).
- Review cadence: Major guides reviewed quarterly; quickstarts reviewed after each SDK release or when CI tests fail.
- Reviewers: Marcus Lee (SDK), Priya Nair (Docs platform), Diego Ramirez (Support).
- Approval: docs must be approved by at least two reviewers before promoted to published on the docs site.

Standards and Structure (required for all published DevEx docs)

Every published doc must include the following sections (use these headers in this order):
1) Title and short description (1-2 sentences).
2) Audience and prerequisites (OS, network, API key scope).
3) Quickstart or TL;DR code sample.
4) Full step-by-step guide with commands and expected outputs.
5) Troubleshooting / top issues table with canonical fixes.
6) Related pages and links (SDK reference, changelog, release notes).
7) Owner and last updated date.

Metadata (example front-matter to include on new templates)

- title: short descriptive title
- description: one-line summary
- languages: list (python, node, curl, go)
- sdk_version: pinned minor version for the sample
- created_by: author name
- last_updated: YYYY-MM-DD

Templates and Naming Conventions

- File names: short, kebab-case, include a year when stable (e.g., sdk-python-quickstart-2026.json).
- Use the following template metadata at the top of each doc (visible in editors):
  * owner_team: engineering
  * labels: sdk, quickstart, tutorial (add service-specific tags as needed)

Canonical Templates (saved in /quickstarts-and-templates)

We maintain the following starter templates. Use them as the basis for new language/feature quickstarts: 

| filename | purpose | owner | tags |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| sdk-python-quickstart-template-2026.json | Minimal Python SDK quickstart (auth, generate) | DevEx | python, quickstart |
| sdk-node-quickstart-template-2026.json | Minimal Node SDK quickstart | DevEx | node, quickstart |
| api-curl-quickstart-template-2026.json | curl-based API examples for shell users | DevEx | curl, api-examples |
| sdk-embeddings-example-template-2026.json | Embeddings end-to-end example (indexing -> query) | DevEx | embeddings, tutorial |

Quickstarts: required content and CI checks

Every quickstart must: 
- Complete in under 5 minutes on a developer machine with minimal setup.
- Include a TL;DR code block at the top and a full walkthrough below.
- Include a single CLI command that validates success (e.g., a test request that returns 200 and expected keys).
- Be accompanied by an automated smoke test in the docs repo that runs the example and verifies output.

Example TL;DR (Python):

from redwood import RedwoodClient
client = RedwoodClient(api_key=\"$REDWOOD_API_KEY\")
resp = client.generate(prompt=\"Say hello\", model=\"redwood-1-medium\")
print(resp.choices[0].text)

Example TL;DR (curl):

curl -sS -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \\\n  -H \"Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY\" \\\n  -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \\\n  -d '{\"model\":\"redwood-1-medium\",\"prompt\":\"Say hello\",\"max_tokens\":8}'

API Examples and Best Practices

- Provide 3 canonical examples per endpoint: minimal, streaming (if supported), and structured-output (JSON schema / function calling).
- Include expected response snippets and response field descriptions (token_count, latency_ms, model_version, request_id).
- Show error handling patterns (retries with exponential backoff for 5xx, immediate fail for 4xx).

Docs Site Operating Procedures

1) Branching and publishing
   - Author creates a feature branch named docs/<area>/<short-desc>.
   - Open a PR to main/docs with the doc file and smoke tests.
   - CI runs: spellcheck, markdownlint, example smoke tests.
   - After 2 approvals (one must be a reviewer listed above), merge into main/docs.
   - Publishing pipeline (nightly) deploys updates to staging site; on-call Docs lead triggers a production deploy after smoke tests pass.

2) Emergency change process
   - For critical fixes (regression or security): open an urgent PR and add label urgent/docs-patch.
   - Pager: DevEx on-call will be paged; patch is fast-tracked with at least one reviewer approval.

Top Support Issues and Canonical Fixes (current list)

These are the most common support tickets for SDKs and the canonical fixes that should be applied in order (document must include an identical troubleshooting section).

1) Authentication errors (401 / invalid_api_key)
   - Symptom: \"401 Unauthorized\" or \"invalid_api_key\" in response.
   - Canonical fix:
     a) Confirm environment variable REDWOOD_API_KEY is set and exported in the shell.
     b) Verify the key has the correct scope in the Console (check tokens -> scopes).
     c) Use the test token provided in the quickstart to reproduce locally.
     d) If token rotation suspected, generate a new token and confirm.

2) Request timeout or connection reset when using streaming
   - Symptom: Partial or no streaming response, socket closed.
   - Canonical fix:
     a) Confirm client library version supports streaming for the model version used.
     b) Check network (corporate proxies) for WebSocket/HTTP2 blocking.
     c) Increase client-side timeout to 60s for long initial responses.
     d) Fall back to non-streaming call in the quickstart to verify the service is reachable.

3) High token usage / unexpected cost spikes
   - Symptom: Customers report unexpectedly high cost after running generation at scale.
   - Canonical fix:
     a) Verify max_tokens and temperature in examples; set conservative defaults (max_tokens=256, temperature=0.7).
     b) Add examples that show token counting and truncation strategies (prefix caching).
     c) Recommend batching and caching strategies from Redwood Optimize.

4) Model mismatch / versioning issues
   - Symptom: Example uses model alias that no longer resolves or behavior differs.
   - Canonical fix:
     a) Always pin examples to a versioned model alias (e.g., redwood-1-medium@2025-10-01) for reproducibility.
     b) Include a short note on how to migrate to recommended alias.

5) CORS failures for browser examples
   - Symptom: Browser console shows CORS errors when calling the API directly.
   - Canonical fix:
     a) Teach recommended pattern: proxy requests through a backend service with token handling.
     b) Provide a minimal proxy example in Node (express) with sample code in the quickstart.

Troubleshooting table (to include in each quickstart)

| symptom | quick-checks | canonical-fix | related doc |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 401 / invalid_api_key | echo $REDWOOD_API_KEY; curl auth endpoint | rotate/regenerate token; check scopes | security-and-compliance/rbac-and-auth |
| partial streaming | use non-stream call; check SDK version | increase timeout; verify proxies | eng-developer-experience/quickstarts-and-templates |

CI and Smoke Tests

- Each quickstart must include a non-flaky smoke test and be added to the docs CI job. Tests should:
  1) Run the TL;DR example with a test token (sandbox)
  2) Validate HTTP status and presence of expected fields (choices/text or embeddings/vector length)
  3) Run in under 30s in CI.

Onboarding checklist for new SDK docs contributor

1) Fork the docs repo and pull latest main/docs.
2) Pick an existing template and update language-specific snippets.
3) Add a smoke test in /tests/docs-examples/ matching existing patterns.
4) Add labels and metadata in front-matter.
5) Request reviews from DevEx reviewers and address feedback.

Metrics and SLAs for DevEx docs

- Coverage metric: 90% of public endpoints should have a quickstart and one language example.
- Mean time to publish a critical fix: < 24 hours after detection.
- Support load: aim to reduce repeat tickets for identical issues by 40% YoY via canonical fixes.

Appendix: Example Node proxy for browser quickstart

// minimal express proxy to avoid exposing API keys in browser
const express = require('express');
const fetch = require('node-fetch');
const app = express();
app.use(express.json());
app.post('/v1/proxy/generate', async (req, res) => {
  const r = await fetch('https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate', {
    method: 'POST',
    headers: { 'Authorization': `Bearer ${process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY}`, 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
    body: JSON.stringify(req.body)
  });
  const body = await r.text();
  res.status(r.status).send(body);
});
app.listen(3000, () => console.log('proxy listening on 3000'))

Contact / escalation

- Primary owner: Ava Thompson (DevEx) — ava@redwood.ai
- Support escalation: file a ticket with Support -> include doc version, smoke test ID, and an example request/response.
- For platform regressions, tag eng-platform and eng-serving-runtime on the PR.
